terms.definition: A species that donates a proton, H⁺.
terms.examiner: A Brønsted–Lowry base accepts a proton.

terms.definition: Two species that can be interconverted by the transfer of a proton.
terms.examiner: Label the pairs as acid 1/base 1 and acid 2/base 2: each pair differs by one H⁺.

terms.definition: An acid that dissociates completely in aqueous solution.
terms.examiner: A weak acid dissociates only partially. Strength is not the same as concentration.
Give pH to two decimal places unless told otherwise.

terms.definition: Ka = [H⁺][A⁻] ÷ [HA] for a weak acid HA. pKa = –log Ka.
terms.examiner: The larger the Ka (the smaller the pKa), the stronger the acid. The approximations are that [H⁺] = [A⁻] and that [HA] at equilibrium equals its original concentration.
Use it to find the pH of a strong base: [H⁺] = Kw ÷ [OH⁻].

terms.definition: A system that minimises pH changes on the addition of small amounts of an acid or a base.
terms.examiner: "Minimises", not "prevents". Made from a weak acid and its salt, or from excess weak acid and a strong alkali.

terms.definition: The point in a titration at which the acid and base have reacted exactly in the mole ratio of the equation.
terms.examiner: It is the centre of the vertical section of the pH curve. An indicator is suitable if its pH range lies within that vertical section.
